name: AL-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans about seventeen points Republican after redistricting
Jerry Carl holds a massive fundraising edge ($1.44M raised and $547K outside support vs. $184K for Jones)
Prediction markets price a Republican win near 96 percent
No public polls or expert ratings treat the race as competitive
model.rationale: The district's seventeen-point Republican lean, Carl's overwhelming financial advantage in both direct fundraising and outside support, and prediction markets pricing a Republican win near 96 percent all point the same direction, with no polling or ratings suggesting competition.
model.watch: Any general-election polling, a late outside-spending surge for Jones, or an unexpected scandal could widen the uncertainty, though a genuinely competitive race would require an unusual shift in this electorate.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's first district is an open seat after redistricting reshuffled the map, and it remains firmly Republican territory with a partisan lean of roughly seventeen points toward the GOP. Jerry Carl, who represented the area before the new lines, enters the general election with a decisive financial edge: about $1.4 million raised and more than half a million dollars in outside support, against roughly $184,000 for Democrat Clyde Jones Jr. No independent public polls cover the race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive.

Prediction markets give the Democratic nominee only about a three percent chance, consistent with the district's fundamentals. With a large money gap, a favorable electorate, and no visible Democratic campaign infrastructure, the seat is rated safe for Republicans, though the absence of polling leaves some residual uncertainty.
